title: CSS
tagline: Style the web: from selectors and the box model to Grid, animations and modern CSS.
description: A complete CSS revision track that goes from the very basics (selectors, colors, box model) through layout (Flexbox, Grid, positioning) and responsive design, to animations, modern CSS features (custom properties, cascade layers, container queries) and architecture. Every topic has runnable examples, key points, pitfalls and interview questions.

topics.title: What is CSS and How to Add It
topics.summary: CSS controls how HTML looks; learn the rule syntax and the three ways to attach styles.
topics.description:
**CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)** describes how HTML elements are presented: colors, fonts, spacing, layout and animation. HTML gives the page *structure and meaning*; CSS gives it *looks*. Keeping them separate means you can restyle a whole site by editing one file.

### Anatomy of a rule

```css
selector {
  property: value;
  another-property: value;
}
```

- **Selector** chooses which elements to style (`h1`, `.card`, `#btn`).
- **Declaration** is one `property: value;` pair.
- A rule can hold many declarations inside `{ }`.

### Three ways to add CSS

| Method | Where | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| Inline | `style="..."` attribute | Quick tests, dynamic values from JS |
| Internal | `<style>` in `<head>` | Single page demos |
| External | `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">` | Real projects (cacheable, reusable) |

External CSS is the best choice: the browser caches the file and every page shares it.

### Comments and values
Comments are written as `/* ... */`. Values can be keywords (`red`, `center`), numbers with units (`16px`), colors (`#ff3368`), functions (`rgb()`, `calc()`) and more.

### Why "Cascading"?
When several rules target the same element, the browser decides which one wins using the **cascade**: origin, importance, specificity and order. You will study this in detail in the next topics.

### Practice idea
Take any plain HTML page, link a `style.css` file and change the heading color and the link hover color. That is exactly what the first lesson of this course does: `h1 { color: #ff3368; }` and `#btn:hover { background-color: black; }`.

interview.a: Inline (style attribute), internal (<style> tag in head) and external (<link> to a .css file). External is preferred because it is cached and reusable.

topics.summary: Pick exactly the elements you want: element, class, id, universal, group and attribute selectors.
topics.description:

elements | | Class | `.card` | elements with `class="card"` | | ID | `#header` | the one element with `id="header"` | | Group | `h1, h2, h3` | any of the listed selectors | ### Attribute selectors Match elements by their attributes: ```css a[target] { } /* has the attribute */ a[target="_blank"] { } /* exact value */ a[href^="https"] { } /* starts with */ a[href$=".pdf"] { } /* ends with */ a[href*="google"] { } /* contains */ input[type="checkbox"] { } ``` ### Class vs ID - A **class** is reusable: many elements, many classes per element. - An **id** must be unique per page and has very high specificity, so avoid styling with ids. ### Combining You can chain selectors without spaces to require all conditions: `a.btn.primary` means an that has both classes. topics.title: Colors
topics.summary: Named colors, HEX, RGB, HSL, alpha transparency, currentColor and modern color functions.
topics.description:
CSS lets you write the same color in many notations. Pick the one that is easiest to read and adjust.

### Notations

| Notation | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Named | `tomato` | 140+ keywords |
| HEX | `#ff0000` / `#f00` | most common in design tools |
| RGB | `rgb(255 0 0)` | red, green, blue 0-255 |
| RGBA | `rgba(255,0,0,0.5)` | last value is alpha 0-1 |
| HSL | `hsl(0 100% 50%)` | hue (0-360deg), saturation, lightness |
| HSLA | `hsl(0 100% 50% / 0.5)` | HSL with alpha |

### Why HSL?
HSL is human friendly. Keep the hue and change only lightness to get a darker or lighter shade of the same color - perfect for hover states and themes.

### Transparency
- **alpha** in `rgba()`/`hsla()` only fades that color.
- **opacity** fades the whole element including children.
- `transparent` is a keyword for fully transparent (`rgba(0,0,0,0)`).

### currentColor
`currentColor` takes the current value of the element's `color` property. It is great for borders, icons (SVG `fill: currentColor`) and underline colors so they follow the text color automatically.

### Modern color
Newer browsers support `oklch()`, `color-mix()` and the `light-dark()` function. `color-mix(in srgb, red 30%, white)` blends colors without a preprocessor.

### Accessibility
Keep a contrast ratio of at least **4.5:1** for normal text (WCAG AA). Never use color as the only way to show information.

topics.title: Units: px, %, em, rem, vw, vh
topics.summary: Absolute vs relative units and when to use px, em, rem, %, vw, vh, ch and fr.
topics.description:
CSS units define sizes. They fall into **absolute** and **relative** units.

### Absolute
- **px** - one CSS pixel. Predictable, good for borders, small shadows, hairlines.
- cm, mm, in, pt - mostly for print.

### Relative
| Unit | Relative to | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `%` | parent's size (width) or containing block | fluid widths |
| `em` | font-size of the **parent** (or the element itself when used outside font-size) | padding inside components |
| `rem` | font-size of the **root** (<html>) | font sizes, spacing, media queries |
| `vw / vh` | 1% of viewport width / height | full-screen sections |
| `dvh / svh / lvh` | dynamic/small/large viewport height | mobile browsers with moving address bar |
| `ch` | width of the "0" character | readable line length: `max-width: 65ch` |
| `fr` | share of free space in Grid | grid columns |

### em compounding
Because `em` is relative to the parent, nested elements multiply: a list inside a list at `1.2em` keeps growing. `rem` avoids this because it always looks at the root.

### The 62.5% trick
Browsers default to `16px`. Setting `html { font-size: 62.5%; }` makes `1rem = 10px`, so `2.4rem` is `24px`. The source course uses this. A safer variant keeps the user's setting: use `100%` and calculate normally.

### Best practices
- Use **rem** for font sizes and spacing so user font-size preferences are respected.
- Use **px** for borders and tiny details.
- Use **%**/`fr` for layout widths.
- Never use `vw` alone for font-size (zoom will not work) - combine it with `clamp()`.

topics.title: Cascade, Inheritance and Initial Values
topics.summary: How the browser picks winning declarations and which properties flow down to children.
topics.description:
Two big ideas explain most "why is my style not applied?" problems: the **cascade** and **inheritance**.

### The cascade
When many declarations target one property of one element, the browser picks a winner in this order:

1. **Origin and importance** - user-agent styles < author styles; `!important` reverses the order.
2. **Cascade layers** (`@layer`) - later layers win; unlayered styles beat layered ones.
3. **Specificity** - more specific selector wins.
4. **Source order** - if still tied, the last declaration wins.

### Inheritance
Some properties pass from parent to child automatically:

- **Inherited**: `color`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height`, `text-align`, `visibility`, `cursor`, `list-style`.
- **Not inherited**: `margin`, `padding`, `border`, `background`, `width`, `height`, `display`, `position`.

### Control keywords
| Keyword | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inherit` | take the parent's value |
| `initial` | the CSS spec default value |
| `unset` | inherit if the property is inheritable, otherwise initial |
| `revert` | go back to the browser's default stylesheet |
| `revert-layer` | go back to the previous cascade layer |

### The `all` shorthand
`all: unset;` resets every property of an element, useful when building isolated components.

### Computed value flow
Specified value -> computed value -> used value -> actual value. The DevTools "Computed" tab shows the final result and which rule won.

topics.title: Specificity
topics.summary: The scoring system that decides which selector wins when rules conflict.
topics.description:
**Specificity** is a weight the browser assigns to every selector. If two rules set the same property on the same element, the rule with the higher specificity wins - regardless of order.

### Hierarchy (low to high)
1. Element selectors and pseudo-elements: `h1`, `::before`
2. Classes, attributes and pseudo-classes: `.card`, `[type="text"]`, `:hover`
3. IDs: `#navbar`
4. Inline styles: `style="..."`
5. `!important` (beats everything in the normal origin)

### Scoring as (ID, CLASS, ELEMENT)

| Selector | Score |
|---|---|
| `p` | 0,0,1 |
| `.hero-content p` | 0,1,1 |
| `#main .item a:hover` | 1,2,1 |
| `a.btn:not(.x)` | 0,2,1 |

Compare left to right: any ID beats any number of classes; any class beats any number of elements. (Think of it as digits in separate columns, not a base-10 number.)

### Notes
- The universal selector `*` and combinators (`>`, `+`, `~`) add **zero**.
- `:is()` takes the specificity of its most specific argument; `:where()` always adds **zero**; `:not()` counts its argument.
- Equal specificity: **later rule wins**.

### Writing maintainable CSS
- Prefer single class selectors (0,1,0).
- Avoid ids and deep descendant chains.
- Avoid `!important`; use it only for utilities or to override third-party CSS.
- Use `@layer` or `:where()` to keep base styles easy to override.

topics.title: The Box Model
topics.summary: Every element is a box made of content, padding, border and margin.
topics.description:
In CSS **every element is a rectangular box**. The box model describes the layers of that box from the inside out:

1. **Content** - the text, image or children.
2. **Padding** - space between the content and the border (inside the box, shows the background).
3. **Border** - the line around the padding.
4. **Margin** - transparent space outside the border that separates the element from its neighbours.

### Size calculation (default `content-box`)
`width` and `height` set only the **content** area. The visible size is:

```text
total width = width + padding-left + padding-right + border-left + border-right
```

For example, `width: 800px; padding: 50px; border: 20px solid;` gives a box that occupies **940px** horizontally (800 + 100 + 40). Margin is added on top of this for spacing, but it is not part of the box background.

### Block vs inline boxes
- **Block** boxes take the full available width and start on a new line, and respect all four margins/paddings and width/height.
- **Inline** boxes flow in a line; width/height are ignored and vertical margins have no effect.

### Inspecting the box
Open DevTools, pick an element and look at the **Box Model diagram** in the Computed tab: it shows the content, padding, border and margin values in different colors. This is the fastest way to debug unexpected spacing.

### Why it matters
Almost every layout bug ("why is it 20px too wide?", "why does it overflow?") comes from forgetting that padding and border are added to width. The next topic (`box-sizing`) fixes this.

interview.q: Explain the CSS box model.
interview.a: Each element is a box with content, padding, border and margin layers. width/height apply to the content box by default; padding and border are added around it and margin sits outside.

interview.q: Do inline elements respect width and height?
interview.a: No. Width/height and vertical margins are ignored on non-replaced inline elements; use inline-block or block.

interview.q: Is margin part of the element's size?
interview.a: No. Margin is outside the border, is transparent and is not painted with the background, but it affects the space the element takes in layout.

topics.title: box-sizing and CSS Reset
topics.summary: border-box makes width include padding and border; a reset gives a predictable starting point.
topics.description:
`box-sizing` controls what `width` and `height` mean.

| Value | width applies to | 300px wide + 20px padding + 5px border |
|---|---|---|
| `content-box` (default) | content only | 350px on screen |
| `border-box` | content + padding + border | **300px** on screen |

`border-box` is far easier to reason about: the number you write is the size you get. That is why almost every project starts with:

```css
*,
*::before,
*::after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
```

### Inherit pattern (friendly to third-party widgets)
```css
html { box-sizing: border-box; }
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: inherit; }
```

### What is a CSS reset?
Browsers ship default styles (body margin 8px, h1 margins, list bullets). A **reset** removes or normalises them so you start from the same baseline in every browser.

- **Classic reset**: `* { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }` (used in the source course).
- **Normalize.css**: keeps useful defaults but fixes inconsistencies.
- **Modern reset**: small and opinionated, e.g. `img { max-width: 100%; display: block; }`, `body { line-height: 1.5; }`, form controls `font: inherit;`.

### Tips
- Do not reset `*` margin if you rely on default heading spacing - then your own spacing rules must replace them.
- A tiny reset is usually enough. Do not copy huge resets without understanding them.

topics.title: Margin
topics.summary: Space outside an element: shorthand, auto centering, negative margins and margin collapsing.
topics.description:
**Margin** creates space *outside* the border. It pushes neighbouring elements away.

### Shorthand
| Values | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `margin: 10px` | all sides |
| `margin: 10px 20px` | top/bottom, left/right |
| `margin: 10px 20px 30px` | top, left/right, bottom |
| `margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px` | top, right, bottom, left (clockwise) |

Individual sides: `margin-top`, `margin-right`, `margin-bottom`, `margin-left`.

### margin: auto
On a block element with a set `width`, `margin: 0 auto;` centers it horizontally. Inside flex/grid, auto margins absorb free space (`margin-left: auto` pushes an item to the right).

### Negative margins
Allowed. They pull an element toward or over its neighbours - useful for overlaps and gutter tricks, but use sparingly.

### Margin collapsing
Vertical margins of **adjacent block siblings** collapse into the **larger one** (not the sum). A parent and its first/last child can collapse too if there is no padding, border or clearfix between them. Collapsing does **not** happen in flex or grid containers, with floats, absolutely positioned elements or `overflow` other than visible.

Ways to avoid surprises:
- use one-direction spacing (only `margin-bottom` or use `gap`),
- add `padding` or `border` to the parent,
- use `display: flow-root` on the parent.

### Logical margins
`margin-inline` and `margin-block` adapt to writing direction (see Logical Properties).

interview.q: What is margin collapsing?
interview.a: When vertical margins of adjacent block elements (or parent and child) meet, they combine into a single margin equal to the largest one instead of adding up.

interview.q: How do you center a block element horizontally?
interview.a: Give it a width and set margin-left and margin-right to auto (margin: 0 auto).

interview.q: Can margins be negative?
interview.a: Yes. Negative margins pull the element toward neighbours or make it overlap them.

interview.q: Which situations prevent margin collapse?
interview.a: Flex/grid items, floats, absolutely positioned boxes, inline-block, and parents that establish a new block formatting context (display: flow-root, overflow: auto).

topics.title: Padding
topics.summary: Space inside the border: shorthand, buttons and cards, and why negative padding does not exist.
topics.description:
**Padding** is the space between the content and the border, *inside* the element. The element's background and background image extend under the padding.

### Shorthand (same as margin)
- `padding: 10px;` all sides
- `padding: 5px 10px;` vertical | horizontal
- `padding: 1px 2px 2px;` top | horizontal | bottom
- `padding: 5px 1px 0 2px;` top | right | bottom | left

Individual: `padding-top`, `padding-right`, `padding-bottom`, `padding-left`.

### Differences from margin
| | padding | margin |
|---|---|---|
| Location | inside border | outside border |
| Background | painted | transparent |
| Negative values | **not allowed** | allowed |
| auto | not allowed | allowed |
| Collapses | never | vertical margins can |
| Clickable area | yes (part of element) | no |

### Typical uses
- Buttons: `padding: 12px 36px;` gives a comfortable click area.
- Cards and panels: `padding: 24px;` separates text from the edge.
- Making inline links bigger tap targets (`display: inline-block; padding: ...`).

topics.summary: border shorthand, individual sides, border-radius shapes and the outline property.
topics.description:
### Border shorthand
`border: <width> <style> <color>;` for example `border: 2px solid #333;`.

Individual properties: `border-width`, `border-style`, `border-color`. Per side: `border-top`, `border-right`, `border-bottom`, `border-left` and even `border-top-width` etc.

**Styles**: `none`, `hidden`, `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `inset`, `outset`. Without a style the border does not show!

Multiple values follow the usual clockwise rule: `border-style: dotted solid;` (top/bottom dotted, left/right solid).

### border-radius
Rounds the corners.

- `border-radius: 10px;` all corners
- `border-radius: 10px 20%;` top-left+bottom-right | top-right+bottom-left
- `border-radius: 15px 5px 10px 20px;` TL | TR | BR | BL
- `border-radius: 50%;` circle (on a square) or ellipse
- `border-radius: 999px;` pill shape
- Elliptical: `border-radius: 100% 0 / 100% 0;` horizontal / vertical radii

### Logical border shorthands
`border-inline` (left+right) and `border-block` (top+bottom) are newer shorthands: `border-block: 5px solid red;`.

### outline
`outline` draws a line **outside** the border, does not take space and does not follow border-radius in older browsers. Perfect for focus rings: `outline: 3px solid #2965f1; outline-offset: 2px;`.

### Other border tricks
- Triangles with zero-size box and transparent borders.
- `border-image` for gradient or image borders.
- Gradient borders: `border: 4px solid transparent; background: linear-gradient(...) border-box;`.

topics.title: Overflow
topics.summary: Control what happens when content is bigger than its box: visible, hidden, scroll, auto and clip.
topics.description:
When content does not fit in its box it **overflows**. The `overflow` property decides what the browser does.

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `visible` | default; content spills outside the box |
| `hidden` | extra content is clipped, no scrollbars (but can still scroll programmatically) |
| `scroll` | scrollbars are always shown |
| `auto` | scrollbars only when needed - the usual choice |
| `clip` | like hidden but no scrolling at all and no new formatting context |

Control each axis: `overflow-x` and `overflow-y`. If one is not `visible`, the other cannot stay visible (it becomes `auto`).

### Common patterns
- **Scrollable panel**: fixed `height` / `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto`.
- **Horizontal scroller**: `overflow-x: auto; white-space: nowrap;` (as in the source demo).
- **Clipping children to rounded corners**: `border-radius` + `overflow: hidden`.
- **Clearing floats / containing margins**: `overflow: auto` or better `display: flow-root`.

### Text overflow
```css
.truncate {
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;   /* adds ... */
}
```
Multi-line clamp: `display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 3; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;` (also standard `line-clamp` is arriving).

### Nice scrolling extras
- `scroll-behavior: smooth;`
- `overscroll-behavior: contain;` to stop scroll chaining
- `scrollbar-gutter: stable;` to avoid layout shift
- `scrollbar-width: thin;`

topics.title: Text Properties
topics.summary: Align, decorate, transform and space text; shadows, white-space and drop caps.
topics.description:
CSS has many properties dedicated to how text looks and flows.

### Alignment and decoration
- `text-align`: `left`, `right`, `center`, `justify`.
- `text-decoration`: shorthand for `-line` (underline, overline, line-through), `-color`, `-style` (solid, double, dotted, wavy) and `-thickness`. `text-decoration: none` removes link underlines.
- `text-underline-offset` moves the underline away from the text.
- `text-transform`: `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize`.
- `text-indent` indents the first line.

### Spacing
| Property | Controls |
|---|---|
| `letter-spacing` | space between characters |
| `word-spacing` | space between words |
| `line-height` | distance between lines - use a unitless number like `1.6` |

### white-space and wrapping
- `white-space: nowrap` keeps text on one line.
- `white-space: pre-wrap` preserves line breaks and spaces.
- `overflow-wrap: anywhere` / `word-break: break-word` break long words.
- `text-wrap: balance` (modern) evens out heading lines.

### text-shadow
`text-shadow: x y blur color;` e.g. `text-shadow: 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);`. Multiple shadows are comma separated (useful for glow).

### Gradient text
```css
.gradient { background: linear-gradient(90deg,#f06,#48f); -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }
```

### Readability tips
- Line length around 45-75 characters (`max-width: 65ch`).
- `line-height` 1.5 to 1.7 for body text.
- Do not justify text on narrow columns (it creates rivers of white space).

topics.title: Fonts and Font Properties
topics.summary: font-family stacks, size, weight, style, shorthand and web-safe fallbacks.
topics.description:
### Main font properties
| Property | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `font-family` | `"Urbanist", Arial, sans-serif` | list of fonts, last should be a generic family |
| `font-size` | `1.125rem` | prefer rem |
| `font-weight` | `400`, `700`, `bold` | numeric 100-900 |
| `font-style` | `normal` / `italic` / `oblique` | |
| `font-variant` | `small-caps` | |
| `line-height` | `1.5` | |

### Font stack and fallbacks
If the first font is missing, the browser tries the next. Always end with a **generic family**: `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `cursive`, `system-ui`.

```css
body {
  font-family: "Urbanist", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
}
```

Quote font names that contain spaces.

### Shorthand
`font: italic small-caps 700 1.25rem/1.5 "Poppins", sans-serif;` - order: style, variant, weight, size/line-height, family. Size and family are **required**.

### Loading fonts
- **Google Fonts**: `<link>` in head (or `@import` - slower).
- **Self hosted**: `@font-face` (see the Fonts and Variable Fonts topic).
- Use `font-display: swap;` to avoid invisible text while the font loads.

### Good practice
- 1-2 font families per site.
- Use a system font stack for speed.
- Set `font-family` once on `body` and let it inherit. Form controls do not inherit by default, so add `button, input { font: inherit; }`.

topics.title: Backgrounds
topics.summary: background-color, image, repeat, position, size, attachment, clip and multiple backgrounds.
topics.description:
The background layer paints behind the content, padding and border.

### Longhand properties
| Property | Common values |
|---|---|
| `background-color` | any color |
| `background-image` | `url(...)`, gradients; comma-separated for multiple layers |
| `background-repeat` | `repeat`, `no-repeat`, `repeat-x`, `repeat-y`, `space`, `round` |
| `background-position` | `center`, `top left`, `50% 20%`, `right 10px bottom 10px` |
| `background-size` | `auto`, `cover`, `contain`, `100% 100%` |
| `background-attachment` | `scroll`, `fixed`, `local` |
| `background-clip` | `border-box`, `padding-box`, `content-box`, `text` |
| `background-origin` | where the position box starts |

### cover vs contain
- `cover`: scale so the image fills the box completely (may crop).
- `contain`: scale so the whole image is visible (may leave gaps).

### Multiple backgrounds
Layers are comma separated and the **first one is on top**:

```css
background:
  linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.5), rgba(0,0,0,.5)),  /* overlay on top */
  url("photo.jpg") center / cover no-repeat;
```

### Shorthand
`background: color image repeat position / size attachment;` - note the slash between position and size.

### Parallax-like effect
`background-attachment: fixed;` keeps the image still while the page scrolls (used in the project in this course). It is not supported well on mobile.

### Blend modes
`background-blend-mode: multiply;` mixes layers with each other and with the background color.

topics.title: Gradients
topics.summary: linear, radial, conic and repeating gradients, color stops and overlays.
topics.description:
A **gradient** is an image generated by CSS, used with `background-image` (or `background`). No image file is needed and it scales perfectly.

### linear-gradient
```css
background: linear-gradient(to right, red, yellow);
background: linear-gradient(135deg, #004d7a, #00bf72, #a8eb12);
background: linear-gradient(to bottom right, #004d7a 0%, #a8eb12 100%);
```
Direction can be a keyword (`to top left`) or an angle (`90deg` = to right, `0deg` = to top).

### radial-gradient
Starts at a center point and spreads outward.
```css
background: radial-gradient(circle at center, #ff5733 0%, #ffc300 40%, #2980b9 100%);
```
Shape: `circle` or `ellipse` (default). Size keywords: `closest-side`, `farthest-corner`.

### conic-gradient
Colors rotate around a center - great for pie charts and color wheels:
```css
background: conic-gradient(red, yellow, lime, aqua, blue, magenta, red);
```

### Color stops
- Add positions: `red 20%, blue 60%`.
- Two stops at the same position make a **hard edge**: `red 50%, blue 50%`.
- Use transparency (`rgba(255,0,0,0)`) for fades.

### Repeating gradients
`repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #d2e0fb 0 10px, #79ac78 10px 20px)` makes stripes.

### Overlay trick
Put a semi-transparent gradient above an image to darken it for readable text:
`background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.5), rgba(0,0,0,.5)), url(photo.jpg);`

### Tips
- Gradients are images: use `background-size` to make patterns.
- Use `in oklch` (e.g. `linear-gradient(in oklch, blue, red)`) for smoother mixes in modern browsers.

topics.summary: Style bullets with list-style and links with :link, :visited, :hover, :active (LVHA order).
topics.description:
### Lists
- `list-style-type`: `disc`, `circle`, `square`, `decimal`, `lower-alpha`, `none`...
- `list-style-position`: `outside` (default) or `inside`.
- `list-style-image`: use an image as a marker.
- `list-style`: shorthand, e.g. `list-style: square inside;`.

Remove bullets for navigation menus: `ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }`. Custom markers are best done with `li::marker` or `li::before`.

### Counters
CSS counters number any element: `counter-reset`, `counter-increment`, `content: counter(name)`.

### Links and states
Anchors have several states. Style them in **LVHA** order so later ones override earlier ones:

1. `a:link` - unvisited
2. `a:visited` - already visited (only color-like properties allowed for privacy)
3. `a:hover` - mouse over
4. `a:active` - while being clicked

Also remember `:focus` and `:focus-visible` for keyboard users.

### Making a link look like a button
Anchors are inline, so set `display: inline-block;` before giving padding/width:

```css
a.btn { display: inline-block; padding: 10px 32px; border-radius: 5px; text-decoration: none; }
```

### Tips
- Keep underlines on links inside text; users rely on them.
- Provide at least 3:1 contrast between link and surrounding text if you remove underlines.

topics.summary: Make images responsive, crop them with object-fit and keep proportions with aspect-ratio.
topics.description:
### Responsive images
The simplest rule for fluid images:

```css
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
```
- `max-width: 100%` stops overflow.
- `height: auto` keeps the proportions.
- `display: block` removes the tiny gap below inline images.

Always set `width` and `height` attributes in HTML so the browser reserves space and avoids layout shift (CLS).

### object-fit
When an image (or video) has a fixed box, `object-fit` decides how it fills it:

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `fill` | stretches (default) |
| `contain` | fits entirely, may letterbox |
| `cover` | fills and crops, keeps ratio |
| `none` | natural size |
| `scale-down` | smaller of none or contain |

`object-position` chooses the focal point, e.g. `object-position: top;` for portraits.

### aspect-ratio
`aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;` makes a box keep a ratio without padding hacks. Use `aspect-ratio: 1;` for squares/avatars. If both width and height are set, the ratio is ignored.

### Related
- `border-radius: 50%` + `object-fit: cover` = perfect circular avatar.
- `loading="lazy"` and `srcset` / `<picture>` for performance (HTML side).
- `filter` and `clip-path` for effects (see the Visual Effects section).

topics.title: Combinators
topics.summary: Descendant, child, adjacent sibling and general sibling selectors describe relationships.
topics.description:
**Combinators** connect two selectors by their position in the HTML tree.

| Combinator | Syntax | Selects |
|---|---|---|
| Descendant | `A B` (space) | any B inside A, at any depth |
| Child | `A > B` | B that is a **direct** child of A |
| Adjacent sibling | `A + B` | the B immediately after A (same parent) |
| General sibling | `A ~ B` | every B after A (same parent) |
| Universal | `*` | every element (not a combinator but often grouped with them) |

### Examples in practice
```css
nav a            { }   /* every link inside nav */
ul > li          { }   /* only top-level items of that list */
h2 + p           { }   /* the paragraph right after each h2 */
input:checked ~ label { } /* labels after a checked input */
```

### Why child combinator matters
With nested lists, `ul li` also styles the nested items, but `ul > li` only styles the first level. The source course demonstrates this with brown (`.content-1 > ul > li`), pink (`p + li`) and purple (`p ~ li`) colors.

### Sibling combinators
They only look **forward** (later siblings), never backward. For "previous sibling" or "parent" logic use `:has()`.

### Specificity
Combinators add no specificity; only the simple selectors around them count.

### Tips
- Use `>` to avoid accidental deep matches.
- Lobotomized owl: `* + * { margin-top: 1em; }` adds spacing between all siblings except the first.

topics.title: Pseudo-classes
topics.summary: Style elements by state or position: :hover, :focus, :checked, :nth-child() and more.
topics.description:
A **pseudo-class** (single colon `:`) selects an element in a particular *state* or *position*.

### User-action states
- `:hover` pointer is over the element.
- `:active` being pressed.
- `:focus` has keyboard/mouse focus; `:focus-visible` only when the focus ring should show (keyboard).
- `:focus-within` the element or a descendant has focus.

### Form states
`:checked`, `:disabled`, `:enabled`, `:required`, `:optional`, `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:placeholder-shown`, `:read-only`.

### Structural (position)
| Selector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `:first-child` / `:last-child` | first/last among all siblings |
| `:nth-child(n)` | n-th among all siblings |
| `:first-of-type` / `:last-of-type` | first/last of that tag among siblings |
| `:nth-of-type(n)` | n-th of that tag |
| `:only-child` | only child |
| `:empty` | has no children/text |

### nth-child formulas
- `:nth-child(odd)` / `:nth-child(even)`
- `:nth-child(3)` third item
- `:nth-child(3n)` every third
- `:nth-child(n+4)` from the fourth onward
- `:nth-child(-n+3)` only the first three
- `:nth-last-child(2)` counts from the end

### :first-child vs :first-of-type
`p:first-child` matches a paragraph only if it is the **very first child**. `p:first-of-type` matches the first paragraph even if a heading comes before it.

### Other useful ones
`:root` (html element, great for variables), `:target` (element whose id is in the URL hash), `:not()`, `:is()`, `:has()` (next topics).

topics.title: Pseudo-elements
topics.summary: ::before, ::after, ::first-letter, ::first-line, ::selection, ::marker and ::placeholder.
topics.description:
A **pseudo-element** (double colon `::`) styles a *part* of an element or inserts virtual content.

### ::before and ::after
They create a virtual child **before/after** the element's content. They only render if `content` is set (even an empty string).

```css
.title::before { content: "★ "; color: gold; }
.title::after  { content: ""; display: block; width: 60%; border-bottom: 2px solid crimson; }
```

Typical uses: icons, decorative lines, badges, overlays, tooltips, clearfix, CSS shapes and loaders (see the Mini projects).

### Other pseudo-elements
| Pseudo-element | Targets |
|---|---|
| `::first-letter` | first letter (drop caps) |
| `::first-line` | first formatted line |
| `::selection` | highlighted text |
| `::marker` | list bullet/number |
| `::placeholder` | input placeholder text |
| `::backdrop` | behind <dialog>/fullscreen |
| `::file-selector-button` | file input button |

### Positioning trick
Make the parent `position: relative;` and the pseudo-element `position: absolute;` to place it precisely (underline animations, overlays, ribbons).

### Useful facts
- Pseudo-elements are not in the DOM; screen readers may read `content` text, so do not put essential content there.
- `content` accepts strings, `attr(data-label)`, counters and icons (font escape codes like `"\f121"`).
- Interactive effects: animate `::after` width on hover for an underline.

topics.title: Native CSS Nesting
topics.summary: Write child rules inside parent rules with & - no preprocessor needed.
topics.description:
**CSS Nesting** lets you put one rule inside another, like Sass but built into the browser.

```css
.card {
  padding: 1rem;
  background: white;

  & h2 { font-size: 1.5rem; }       /* .card h2 */
  & p + p { margin-top: .5rem; }

  &:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 12px #0003; }  /* .card:hover */
  &.featured { border: 2px solid gold; }     /* .card.featured */
  &::after { content: ""; }                  /* .card::after */

  .dark & { background: #111; }              /* .dark .card */

  @media (width < 600px) {                   /* nested at-rules */
    padding: .5rem;
  }
}
```

### The & symbol
- `&` stands for the parent selector.
- It is **required** when you join without a space (`&:hover`, `&.active`) or place the parent later (`.dark &`).
- Modern browsers also allow nested type selectors without `&` (`h2 { }` inside `.card`), but using `&` is clearer and more compatible.

### Nested media/container queries
You can put `@media`, `@container`, `@supports` and `@layer` directly inside a rule, keeping the responsive code next to the component.

### Specificity
Nested selectors behave like `:is()` on the parent: the parent's most specific selector counts.

### Best practice
- Nest **2-3 levels** at most; deep nesting creates long selectors that are hard to override.
- Nest states (`&:hover`) and modifiers (`&.active`) - it is the biggest win.
- The source final project and float demo use this style (`& h1 { ... }`).

Use &:hover, &.class, &::after for compound selectors

topics.title: Display: block, inline, inline-block, none
topics.summary: How elements flow on the page and how display, visibility and opacity differ.
topics.description:
The `display` property decides the **outer** behaviour (how the element sits among siblings) and the **inner** behaviour (how its children are laid out).

### Core values
| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `block` | starts on a new line, fills the width, accepts width/height/margin/padding |
| `inline` | flows inside text, ignores width/height and vertical margin |
| `inline-block` | flows like inline but accepts width/height/vertical spacing |
| `none` | removed from layout and accessibility tree |
| `flex` / `inline-flex` | flex container |
| `grid` / `inline-grid` | grid container |
| `flow-root` | block that contains floats and stops margin collapse |
| `contents` | element's box disappears, children participate in parent layout |

### Default displays
- Block: `div`, `p`, `h1-h6`, `ul`, `section`, `header`...
- Inline: `span`, `a`, `strong`, `em`, `img` (replaced inline).

### Hiding things - three ways
| Technique | Space kept? | Visible to screen readers? | Can animate? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display: none` | no | no | no |
| `visibility: hidden` | yes | no | yes (discrete) |
| `opacity: 0` | yes | **yes** | yes |

Visually-hidden but accessible text uses the "sr-only" pattern (position absolute, 1px size, clip).

### Inline-block gap
Whitespace between inline-block elements creates a small gap. Fix with flexbox, or `font-size: 0` on the parent.

### Tip
Making links buttons: `a { display: inline-block; padding: 10px 32px; }` - exactly the technique in the source course demo.

topics.title: Position: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky
topics.summary: Move elements out of or relative to normal flow and know which ancestor they are measured from.
topics.description:
`position` controls how an element is placed. Offsets (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, or `inset`) work on any value except `static`.

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `static` | default; normal flow; offsets and z-index ignored |
| `relative` | stays in flow; offsets move it **from its own normal position**; becomes a reference for absolute children |
| `absolute` | removed from flow; positioned against the nearest **positioned ancestor** (or the page) |
| `fixed` | removed from flow; positioned against the **viewport**; stays during scroll |
| `sticky` | acts relative until a scroll threshold, then sticks like fixed inside its container |

### The golden pattern
```css
.parent { position: relative; }          /* reference box */
.badge  { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; }
```

### Centering an absolute element
```css
.child { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 200px; height: 100px; }
/* or */
.child { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }
```

### Fixed
Used for sticky headers, floating "WhatsApp" buttons and modals backdrops: `position: fixed; bottom: 20px; right: 20px;`.

### Sticky
```css
header { position: sticky; top: 0; }
```
Needs a threshold (`top`), a scrolling ancestor and **no `overflow: hidden/auto` on ancestors** between it and the scroller. It never leaves its parent.

### Notes
- Absolute and fixed elements do not take space; neighbours collapse into the gap.
- `inset: 0` is shorthand for top/right/bottom/left: 0.
- Positioned elements can use `z-index`.

Use position: relative on the parent as the anchor

topics.title: z-index and Stacking Contexts
topics.summary: Control which overlapping element is in front and learn why z-index sometimes seems ignored.
topics.description:
`z-index` sets the stacking order of overlapping elements along the z-axis (towards the viewer).

### Rules
- Works on **positioned** elements (`relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`) and on flex/grid items.
- Higher number = in front. Negative numbers go behind the parent's background content.
- Equal values: the later element in the HTML is on top.
- Default `auto` = 0 level.

### Stacking context
A **stacking context** is an isolated layer: children can never escape it. Inside a context their z-index values only compete with each other. A new context is created by:

- root element
- positioned element with z-index not auto
- `opacity < 1`
- `transform`, `filter`, `perspective`, `clip-path`, `mix-blend-mode`
- `isolation: isolate`
- flex/grid item with z-index
- `will-change` for some properties

### Why "z-index: 9999" fails
If an element sits inside a parent context with a lower rank, no value can lift it above elements of a higher sibling context. Fix by changing the **parent**, not the child.

### Good practice
- Keep a small scale with custom properties: `--z-dropdown: 100; --z-modal: 1000; --z-toast: 1100;`.
- Add `isolation: isolate` to components to contain their own stacking.
- Avoid random 99999 numbers.

Higher wins; ties go to later source order

topics.title: Float and Clearfix (Legacy Layout)
topics.summary: Floats wrap text around images and built pre-flexbox layouts; know how to clear them.
topics.description:
`float` pushes an element to the left or right so that inline content (text) wraps around it. Before Flexbox and Grid, floats were used to build whole page layouts - you will meet them in old code and interviews.

### Values
- `float: left;` / `float: right;` / `float: none;`
- `clear: left | right | both;` - make an element move below floats.

### Original purpose: wrapping text
```css
img.avatar { float: left; margin: 0 16px 8px 0; }
```

### Side effect: collapsed parent
Floated children leave normal flow, so the parent may collapse to zero height. Fix it with one of:

```css
.parent { display: flow-root; }      /* modern, best */
.parent::after { content: ""; display: block; clear: both; }  /* classic clearfix */
.parent { overflow: auto; }          /* works but may clip */
```

### Float navbar (from the source course)
A header with a logo floated left (30%) and navigation floated right (70%) with `display: inline-block` list items - a typical legacy pattern. Today, use `display: flex; justify-content: space-between;`.

### When to still use float
- Wrapping text around an image or shape (`shape-outside` for curved wrapping).
- Drop caps.

### Do not use float for
Page layout, columns, centering. Use Flexbox or Grid.

topics.title: Flexbox: The Container
topics.summary: One-dimensional layout: direction, wrapping, justify-content, align-items and gap.
topics.description:
**Flexbox** lays out items in **one dimension** (a row or a column) and distributes space between them. Turn it on with `display: flex;` (or `inline-flex`). The direct children become **flex items**.

### Axes
- **Main axis**: the direction of `flex-direction` (row = horizontal).
- **Cross axis**: perpendicular to the main axis.

### Container properties
| Property | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `flex-direction` | `row`, `row-reverse`, `column`, `column-reverse` | sets main axis |
| `flex-wrap` | `nowrap`, `wrap`, `wrap-reverse` | allow multiple lines |
| `flex-flow` | `row wrap` | shorthand of the two above |
| `justify-content` | `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly` | alignment on **main** axis |
| `align-items` | `stretch`, `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `baseline` | alignment on **cross** axis (one line) |
| `align-content` | same as justify-content | spacing of **multiple lines** (needs wrap) |
| `gap` | `16px` or `row-gap column-gap` | space between items |

### Quick recipes
```css
.center  { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; }
.navbar  { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
.cards   { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 20px; }
.column  { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
```

### Remember
- When `flex-direction: column`, **justify-content works vertically** and align-items horizontally.
- `align-items` needs a container height to show vertical centering.
- Use `gap` instead of margins between items.

topics.title: Flexbox: Item Properties (grow, shrink, basis, order)
topics.summary: Make items flexible with flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, the flex shorthand, order and align-self.
topics.description:
Properties on the **flex items** decide how each one shares the container's space.

| Property | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `flex-grow` | 0 | share of the leftover space the item takes |
| `flex-shrink` | 1 | how much it shrinks when space is short |
| `flex-basis` | auto | starting size before growing/shrinking |
| `order` | 0 | visual order (lower first) |
| `align-self` | auto | override the container's align-items for one item |

### The flex shorthand
`flex: grow shrink basis` - common values:

- `flex: 1;` = `1 1 0%` -> share space equally.
- `flex: auto;` = `1 1 auto` -> grow from content size.
- `flex: none;` = `0 0 auto` -> fixed, no flexibility.
- `flex: 0 0 200px;` -> fixed 200px sidebar.

### Typical layouts
```css
.sidebar { flex: 0 0 240px; }
.main    { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
```

### min-width: 0
Flex items have `min-width: auto`, which stops them shrinking below their content - long text or code can overflow. Add `min-width: 0` (and `overflow: hidden` if needed).

### Auto margins
`margin-left: auto;` pushes an item (and everything after it) to the far end - a neat way to separate a logo from nav links.

### Order and accessibility
`order` changes only visual order; keyboard focus still follows the HTML order. Use it carefully.

topics.title: CSS Grid: Fundamentals
topics.summary: Two-dimensional layout with rows, columns, fr units, repeat(), minmax() and gap.
topics.description:
**CSS Grid** is a **two-dimensional** layout system: it controls rows *and* columns at the same time. Activate it with `display: grid;`. Direct children become grid items.

### Defining tracks
```css
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr;      /* 3 columns */
  grid-template-rows: 100px auto;          /* 2 rows */
  gap: 20px;                               /* row-gap + column-gap */
}
```

### Helpful units and functions
| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fr` | fraction of free space |
| `repeat(3, 1fr)` | three equal columns |
| `minmax(250px, 1fr)` | at least 250px, at most 1fr |
| `min-content` / `max-content` | shrink-wrap to content |
| `auto` | fits content / takes remaining |

### Responsive without media queries
```css
.cards { display: grid; gap: 24px;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)); }
```
- **auto-fill**: creates as many tracks as fit, keeps empty ones.
- **auto-fit**: same, but collapses empty tracks so items stretch.

### Alignment
- `justify-items` / `align-items`: align items inside their cells.
- `justify-content` / `align-content`: align the whole grid inside the container.
- `place-items: center;` is shorthand for centering content in cells.

### Implicit grid
Items beyond the defined tracks create implicit rows. Size them with `grid-auto-rows: 250px;` and flow direction with `grid-auto-flow`.

### Terms
Grid lines, tracks, cells, areas, explicit vs implicit grid.

Using fixed pixel columns that overflow on mobile
Putting grid properties on the items instead of the container

topics.title: CSS Grid: Placement, Areas and Alignment
topics.summary: Position items with line numbers, span, named areas, dense flow and alignment properties.
topics.description:
### Placing items by line
Grid lines are numbered from 1. Negative numbers count from the end (`-1` is the last line).

```css
.item-1 { grid-column: 2 / 4; grid-row: 1 / 3; }
.item-2 { grid-column: 1 / -1; }          /* full width */
.item-3 { grid-column: span 2; }          /* span two tracks */
.item-4 { grid-area: 2 / 2 / 3 / 3; }     /* row-start / col-start / row-end / col-end */
```

### Named template areas
Visual and readable page layouts:

```css
.page {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 220px 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:
    "header  header"
    "sidebar main"
    "footer  footer";
}
header  { grid-area: header; }
aside   { grid-area: sidebar; }
main    { grid-area: main; }
footer  { grid-area: footer; }
```
Use `.` for an empty cell. Redefine `grid-template-areas` in a media query to restructure the page.

### Named lines
`grid-template-columns: [full-start] 1fr [content-start] 960px [content-end] 1fr [full-end];`

### Auto placement
- `grid-auto-flow: row | column | dense` (dense backfills holes).
- `grid-auto-rows` / `grid-auto-columns` size implicit tracks, e.g. `minmax(100px, auto)`.

### Alignment cheat sheet
| Target | Inline axis | Block axis | Both |
|---|---|---|---|
| items in cells | `justify-items` | `align-items` | `place-items` |
| one item | `justify-self` | `align-self` | `place-self` |
| whole grid | `justify-content` | `align-content` | `place-content` |

### Overlap
Items can share cells (same grid-area) and overlap; control with `z-index`.

topics.title: Multi-column Layout
topics.summary: Flow text into newspaper-style columns with column-count, column-width, gap and rule.
topics.description:
The **multi-column** module flows content from one column into the next, like a newspaper. Browsers balance the columns automatically.

### Properties
| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `column-count` | exact number of columns |
| `column-width` | ideal column width; the browser decides the count |
| `columns` | shorthand: `columns: 3` or `columns: 15rem` |
| `column-gap` | space between columns (default 1em) |
| `column-rule` | a line between columns (like border) |
| `column-span` | `all` makes a heading span every column |
| `column-fill` | `balance` (default) or `auto` |

### Example
```css
article {
  column-count: 3;
  column-gap: 50px;
  column-rule: 4px solid red;
  text-align: justify;
}
h2 { column-span: all; }
```

### Preventing awkward breaks
- `break-inside: avoid;` keeps cards/figures from splitting across columns.
- `break-before: column;` forces a new column.

### Responsive behaviour
Prefer `column-width: 18rem;` so the number of columns adapts to the available width without media queries.

### When to use
Long text articles, tag lists, masonry-like card collections (with `break-inside: avoid`). For two-dimensional app layouts use Grid instead.

topics.title: Centering Cheat Sheet
topics.summary: Every reliable way to center horizontally, vertically or both, with when to use each.
topics.description:
"How do you center a div?" is the most famous CSS interview question. Know several methods.

### 1. Grid (shortest)
```css
.parent { display: grid; place-items: center; }
```

### 2. Flexbox
```css
.parent { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; }
```

### 3. Flex + auto margin
```css
.parent { display: flex; }
.child  { margin: auto; }
```

### 4. Absolute + transform
```css
.parent { position: relative; }
.child  { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }
```

### 5. Absolute + inset + margin auto (fixed size child)
```css
.child { position: absolute; inset: 0; margin: auto; width: 200px; height: 100px; }
```

### Other cases
| Need | Solution |
|---|---|
| Center text horizontally | `text-align: center;` on the parent |
| Center a block horizontally | `margin-inline: auto;` + width |
| Center inline-block in a line | `text-align: center;` on parent |
| Center single line vertically | `line-height` = container height |
| Center in viewport | `display:grid; place-items:center; min-height: 100dvh;` |

### Which one to pick?
- Layout containers: **grid** or **flex**.
- Overlays, modals, badges: **absolute + transform** or `inset: 0; margin: auto;`.
- Remember the parent needs a **height** for vertical centering.

topics.title: Flexbox vs Grid: Decision Guide
topics.summary: A practical checklist to choose between Flexbox, Grid, or combining both.
topics.description:
Flexbox and Grid are **complementary**, not competitors. Use this guide.

### Core difference
| | Flexbox | Grid |
|---|---|---|
| Dimension | one (row **or** column) | two (rows **and** columns) |
| Driven by | content (items decide size) | layout (container defines tracks) |
| Wrapping | wrapped lines are independent | all rows share the same column tracks |
| Overlap | hard | easy |
| Best for | components | page and section layouts |

### Choose Flexbox when
- laying out a **row of items**: navbar, toolbar, button group, tags;
- items should **size by content** and share leftover space;
- you need to **center** one thing or push an item with auto margins;
- vertical stacking of a card's inner parts (title, text, button at bottom).

### Choose Grid when
- you need **rows and columns aligned together**: card gallery, dashboards, forms with labels;
- you define the **page skeleton** (header, sidebar, main, footer);
- items must **span** multiple tracks or overlap;
- you want responsive columns via `repeat(auto-fit, minmax())`.

### Combine them
A Grid page layout where each card is a Flex column, and the nav inside the header is a Flex row. Both can be nested freely.

### Quick questions
1. Do I care about both axes? -> Grid.
2. Is the content size deciding the layout? -> Flex.
3. Is it a single line of things with gaps? -> Flex.
4. Do I need an aligned table-like layout? -> Grid.

Page skeleton/galleries/dashboards -> Grid

Both support gap, alignment and wrapping

Using fixed-width Grid tracks that break on small screens

topics.title: Responsive Design and Mobile-first
topics.summary: Viewport meta, fluid layouts, mobile-first workflow and modern responsive patterns.
topics.description:
**Responsive design** means one codebase that adapts to every screen size. It rests on three pillars: flexible layouts, flexible media and media queries.

### 1. The viewport meta tag
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```
Without it, phones render the page at ~980px and shrink it.

### 2. Mobile-first workflow
Write the **small-screen styles first** with no query, then add enhancements with `min-width` queries:

```css
.layout { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }               /* mobile: 1 column */
@media (min-width: 768px)  { .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; } }
@media (min-width: 1100px) { .layout { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); } }
```

Benefits: lighter CSS for phones, simpler overrides, forces focus on content.

### 3. Flexible building blocks
- Widths in `%`, `fr`, `min()`, `max-width` instead of fixed px.
- Images: `max-width: 100%; height: auto;`.
- Typography with `rem` and `clamp()`.
- Grid `auto-fit/minmax` and Flexbox `wrap` for self-adjusting layouts.

### 4. Viewport units
`vw`, `vh`, `dvh` (dynamic - adjusts when mobile toolbars appear), `svh` (small), `lvh` (large). Use `min-height: 100dvh;` for full-screen sections.

### 5. Touch and spacing
- Tap targets at least **44x44px**.
- Do not rely on `:hover` for essential actions.
- Use `@media (hover: hover)` for hover-only effects.

### Testing
Use DevTools device mode, real phones, and resize slowly to find where the layout breaks.

topics.title: calc(), min(), max() and clamp()
topics.summary: Math functions for fluid typography, flexible containers and mixed units.
topics.description:
CSS has built-in math functions that evaluate in the browser.

### calc()
Mix units: `width: calc(100% - 240px);`, `padding: calc(1rem + 2vw);`, `height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-h));`. Operators need spaces around `+` and `-` (not `*` or `/`).

### min() and max()
- `min(100%, 600px)` -> the smaller value: a width that never exceeds 600px (like max-width).
- `max(16px, 2vw)` -> the larger value: a lower bound.

### clamp(min, preferred, max)
Value that scales with the viewport but never goes below min nor above max:

```css
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3.5rem); }
.container { width: clamp(320px, 90%, 1200px); }
.section { padding-block: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 6rem); }
```

Fluid type means **no media queries** for headings.

### Accessibility note
Keep a `rem` part in the preferred value (`1rem + 3vw`). Pure `vw` ignores user zoom and fails WCAG.

### Useful combos
- Full-bleed + centered content: `padding-inline: max(1rem, (100% - 1100px) / 2);`
- Scale spacing with custom properties: `--space: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem);`

### Where they work
Any property that takes a length, percentage, number or angle. They can nest: `clamp(1rem, calc(0.5rem + 2vw), 2rem)` (inner calc is optional).

topics.title: Box Shadow, Text Shadow and Drop Shadow
topics.summary: Add depth with box-shadow, glow with text-shadow and shape-aware filter: drop-shadow().
topics.description:
### box-shadow
`box-shadow: offset-x offset-y blur spread color;` - only the two offsets are required.

```css
box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.15);      /* soft card */
box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px #4861ec;          /* inner ring */
box-shadow: 0 0 60px 20px #ffb000;            /* glow (spread 20px) */
box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #0003, 0 8px 24px #0002; /* layered, more realistic */
```

- **blur** softens, **spread** grows or shrinks the shadow.
- `inset` draws inside the box.
- Shadows follow `border-radius`, take **no layout space** and do not affect surrounding elements.
- Use `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color` as a focus ring that is not clipped.

### text-shadow
`text-shadow: 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.3);` - no spread or inset. Multiple comma-separated shadows give neon or outline effects.

### filter: drop-shadow()
Unlike box-shadow (rectangular), `drop-shadow()` follows the **alpha shape** of the element: transparent PNGs, SVGs, clip-path shapes and ::after triangles.

```css
img { filter: drop-shadow(5px 5px 15px rgba(0,0,0,.4)); }
```
No spread and no inset; the color can be before or after the lengths.

### When to use what
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Card elevation | box-shadow |
| Glow on text | text-shadow |
| Shadow of an icon/PNG/clipped shape | drop-shadow() |

### Performance
Large blurs are expensive when animated. Animate `opacity` of a pseudo-element holding the shadow instead of the shadow itself.

topics.description:
`filter` applies graphical effects to an element and its content. Effects can be chained with spaces.

| Function | Example | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `blur()` | `blur(5px)` | gaussian blur |
| `brightness()` | `brightness(1.5)` | lighter/darker |
| `contrast()` | `contrast(0.8)` | |
| `grayscale()` | `grayscale(1)` | black and white |
| `sepia()` | `sepia(.7)` | warm vintage tone |
| `saturate()` | `saturate(2)` | color intensity |
| `hue-rotate()` | `hue-rotate(90deg)` | shifts hues |
| `invert()` | `invert(1)` | negative |
| `opacity()` | `opacity(.5)` | |

topics.title: Blend Modes: mix-blend-mode and background-blend-mode
topics.summary: Blend overlapping elements or background layers like Photoshop layers.
topics.description:
**Blend modes** control how colors of overlapping layers combine, like layer modes in Photoshop.

### Two properties
| Property | Blends |
|---|---|
| `mix-blend-mode` | the element with whatever is **behind** it |
| `background-blend-mode` | the element's own **background layers** (image + color/gradient) |
| `isolation: isolate` | stops an element's blending from reaching below its group |

### Common modes
- `multiply` - darkens; white disappears (great for shadows and tinting).
- `screen` - lightens; black disappears.
- `overlay`, `soft-light`, `hard-light` - increase contrast.
- `difference`, `exclusion` - inverted-looking effects, good for cursors.
- `darken`, `lighten`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color`, `luminosity`.

### Examples
```css
.hero {
  background-color: #ff3368;
  background-image: url(photo.jpg);
  background-blend-mode: multiply;   /* tinted photo */
}
.title { mix-blend-mode: difference; color: white; } /* text inverts over any background */
```

### Practical uses
- Duotone / tinted hero images with no image editing.
- Text that stays readable over mixed backgrounds (difference).
- Custom cursors and neon overlays (screen / lighten).
- Subtle texture overlays with `multiply` or `soft-light`.

### Notes
- Blend modes create stacking contexts and can affect performance on large layers.
- Always check contrast manually - blending changes colors dynamically.

`clip-path` defines the visible region of an element. Everything outside the shape is hidden (and not clickable).

### Shape functions
| Function | Example |
|---|---|
| `circle()` | `circle(50% at 50% 50%)` |
| `ellipse()` | `ellipse(50% 30% at 50% 50%)` |
| `inset()` | `inset(10px 20px round 12px)` |
| `polygon()` | `polygon(50% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)` triangle |
| `path()` | SVG path string |

```css
/* octagon */
clip-path: polygon(20% 0, 80% 0, 100% 20%, 100% 80%, 80% 100%, 20% 100%, 0 80%, 0 20%);
/* arrow */
clip-path: polygon(40% 0, 40% 20%, 100% 20%, 100% 80%, 40% 80%, 40% 100%, 0 50%);
/* circle */

```

- Hero sections with angled edges.
- Image masks, badges, speech bubbles, arrows, stars.
- **Animation**: transition between two polygons with the **same number of points**.
- Reveal effects: animate `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0)` to `inset(0)`.

- The clipped area also clips shadows; use `filter: drop-shadow()` on a parent wrapper to add a shadow.
- Use online generators (like Clippy) to draw polygon points visually.
- `shape-outside` is the sibling property for wrapping text around a shape.

topics.title: Glassmorphism and Neumorphism Recipes
topics.summary: Two popular UI styles built from transparency, blur and layered shadows.
topics.description:
These are visual **styles**, built from properties you already know.

### Glassmorphism
A frosted-glass card floating over a colorful background.

Ingredients:
1. A vivid/gradient background behind the card.
2. Semi-transparent background: `rgba(255,255,255,.15)`.
3. `backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(150%)`.
4. A thin light border: `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.3)`.
5. Soft shadow: `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.2)`.

### Neumorphism (soft UI)
Elements look extruded from the same-colored surface using **two opposite shadows**: a light one top-left and a dark one bottom-right.

```css
.neu {
  background: #e0e5ec;
  border-radius: 20px;
  box-shadow: 9px 9px 16px #a3b1c6, -9px -9px 16px #ffffff;
}
.neu:active { box-shadow: inset 6px 6px 10px #a3b1c6, inset -6px -6px 10px #fff; }
```

### Cautions (accessibility)
- Glass: ensure text contrast against the *worst* area of the background; add a darker tint if needed.
- Neumorphism: low contrast between element and background - boundaries are hard to see for low-vision users. Use it for decoration, and add clear borders or icons for important controls.
- Provide `@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px))` fallback with a more opaque background.

### Tips
- Keep blur values moderate (8-16px) for performance.
- Use CSS variables so one palette generates both light and dark shadows.

topics.title: 2D Transforms: translate, scale, rotate, skew
topics.summary: Move, resize, rotate and skew elements without affecting layout.
topics.description:
The `transform` property changes how an element is **drawn** without changing the space it occupies in the layout. That makes it perfect (and cheap) for animation.

### Functions
| Function | Example | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `translate(x, y)` | `translate(50px, 20px)` | move; also `translateX/Y` |
| `scale(s)` / `scale(x, y)` | `scale(1.2)` | resize (1 = original) |
| `rotate(angle)` | `rotate(45deg)` | clockwise for positive |
| `skew(x, y)` | `skewX(20deg)` | slant |

### Combine functions
```css
transform: translateX(100px) scale(.5) rotate(45deg);
```
Functions are applied **right to left** in terms of coordinate effect, so order matters (rotate then translate moves along the rotated axis).

### Individual transform properties
Modern browsers also provide separate properties - easier to animate independently:

```css
translate: 100px 20px;
rotate: 45deg;
scale: .5;
```

### transform-origin
The pivot point: `transform-origin: top left;`, `center` (default), `50% 100%`, etc. Pendulums rotate around the top (used in the Newton's cradle project).

### Key facts
- Percent in `translate` refers to the element's **own size** (hence the centering trick `translate(-50%, -50%)`).
- Transforms create a stacking context and a containing block for fixed children.
- Inline elements cannot be transformed - set `display: inline-block` or block.
- Layout does not change: neighbours do not move.

topics.title: 3D Transforms and Perspective
topics.summary: Use perspective, rotateX/Y and preserve-3d to build flip cards and 3D scenes.
topics.description:
CSS can transform elements in 3D space with a few extra properties.

### Core ideas
- **perspective** - distance between the viewer and the z=0 plane. Smaller value = stronger 3D effect.
- **rotateX / rotateY / rotateZ** - rotate around an axis.
- **translateZ** - move toward (+) or away (-) from the viewer.
- **transform-style: preserve-3d** - lets children live in the same 3D space instead of being flattened.
- **backface-visibility: hidden** - hide the back of an element when it is turned around.

### Two ways to set perspective
```css
.scene { perspective: 1000px; }                 /* applies to children (shared vanishing point) */
.item  { transform: perspective(600px) rotateY(30deg); } /* per element */
```
`perspective-origin` moves the vanishing point.

### Flip card recipe
```css
.card { transform-style: preserve-3d; transition: transform .8s; }
.card:hover { transform: rotateY(180deg); }
.front, .back { position: absolute; inset: 0; backface-visibility: hidden; }
.back { transform: rotateY(180deg); }
```

### Tips
- Parent needs perspective; the rotating element needs preserve-3d if it has 3D children.
- `overflow: hidden`, `opacity<1` or `filter` on an element flattens its children (breaks preserve-3d).
- Animate with transforms only - GPU friendly.
- Provide a reduced-motion alternative for big spinning effects.

topics.title: Transitions
topics.summary: Animate property changes smoothly between two states with duration, easing and delay.
topics.description:
A **transition** animates a property from its old value to its new value when the state changes (hover, focus, class toggle by JavaScript...).

### Properties
| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `transition-property` | which properties (`all`, `color`, `transform`...) |
| `transition-duration` | time, e.g. `0.3s` or `300ms` |
| `transition-timing-function` | easing: `ease`, `linear`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`, `cubic-bezier()`, `steps()` |
| `transition-delay` | wait before starting |

### Shorthand
```css
transition: property duration timing-function delay;
transition: background-color .3s ease-in-out, transform .3s ease-out;
```

### Where to put it
Put `transition` on the **base** element (not only on :hover) so the animation works in both directions:

```css
.btn { background: #865dff; transition: all .3s linear; }
.btn:hover { background: #d80032; transform: translateY(-3px); }
```

### What can transition
Only properties with **interpolatable** values: colors, lengths, numbers, transforms, shadows, filters. `display` and `auto` sizes cannot (use `max-height`, `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr` or `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`).

### Best practice
- Animate **transform and opacity** (compositor-friendly) instead of width/height/top/left.
- Avoid `transition: all` in production; list the properties.
- Keep durations 150-400ms for UI feedback.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

topics.title: Keyframe Animations
topics.summary: Define multi-step animations with @keyframes and the animation-* properties.
topics.description:
Transitions need a trigger and only go from A to B. **Animations** can run automatically, loop, and have many steps.

### 1. Define keyframes
```css
@keyframes trip {
  0%   { background: #ffbb5c; transform: translate(0, 0); }
  50%  { background: #000;    transform: translate(200px, 80px); }
  100% { background: #ffbb5c; transform: translate(0, 0); }
}
/* or from { } to { } */
```

### 2. Attach it
| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `animation-name` | the @keyframes name |
| `animation-duration` | length of one cycle |
| `animation-timing-function` | easing per cycle (`linear`, `ease-in-out`, `steps()`) |
| `animation-delay` | wait before start |
| `animation-iteration-count` | number or `infinite` |
| `animation-direction` | `normal`, `reverse`, `alternate`, `alternate-reverse` |
| `animation-fill-mode` | `none`, `forwards`, `backwards`, `both` |
| `animation-play-state` | `running` / `paused` |

Shorthand: `animation: trip 2.5s linear 0s infinite alternate both;`

### fill-mode explained
- `forwards`: keep the last keyframe styles after finishing.
- `backwards`: apply the first keyframe during the delay.
- `both`: both of the above.

### Notes
- No trigger needed - it can run on page load.
- You can have multiple animations: `animation: spin 2s linear infinite, pulse 1s ease-in-out infinite;`
- Use `animation-delay` with negative values to start in the middle.
- JavaScript can pause/restart by toggling classes.
- Animate `transform` and `opacity` for the best performance and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

topics.title: Logical Properties and Writing Modes
topics.summary: Use inline/block instead of left/right/top/bottom so layouts adapt to any writing direction.
topics.description:
Physical properties (`left`, `margin-top`, `width`) assume left-to-right, top-to-bottom text. **Logical properties** map to the **inline** axis (the direction text flows) and **block** axis (where new lines stack), so layouts work for RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew) and vertical scripts.

### Mapping (horizontal-tb, LTR)
| Physical | Logical |
|---|---|
| `width` / `height` | `inline-size` / `block-size` |
| `margin-left` / `margin-right` | `margin-inline-start` / `margin-inline-end` |
| `margin-top` / `margin-bottom` | `margin-block-start` / `margin-block-end` |
| `padding: 0 1rem` | `padding-inline: 1rem` |
| `border-top` + `border-bottom` | `border-block` |
| `left` / `top` | `inset-inline-start` / `inset-block-start` |
| `text-align: left` | `text-align: start` |
| `top/right/bottom/left: 0` | `inset: 0` |

### Shorthands
`margin-inline`, `margin-block`, `padding-inline`, `padding-block`, `border-inline`, `border-block`, `inset-inline`, `inset-block`.

### writing-mode
`writing-mode: horizontal-tb | vertical-rl | vertical-lr;` rotates the flow of text. In vertical mode, `inline-size` becomes the height! (The source demo used `writing-mode: vertical-lr` on a heading.)

### Practical use
```css
.container { max-inline-size: 70ch; margin-inline: auto; padding-block: 2rem; }
.icon + .label { margin-inline-start: .5rem; }  /* flips automatically in RTL */
```

topics.title: Scroll Snap and Smooth Scrolling
topics.summary: Make carousels and full-page sections lock into place with scroll-snap and smooth behavior.
topics.description:
**Scroll snap** makes a scroll container stop at defined positions - ideal for carousels, galleries and slide-style pages, with no JavaScript.

### Container
```css
.scroller {
  display: flex;
  overflow-x: auto;
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;   /* axis + strictness */
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  gap: 1rem;
}
```
- `scroll-snap-type: x | y | both` + `mandatory` or `proximity`.
- `mandatory` always settles on a snap point; `proximity` only if close.

### Items
```css
.slide { flex: 0 0 100%; scroll-snap-align: center; }  /* start | center | end */
```
- `scroll-snap-stop: always;` prevents skipping items on fast swipes.

### Offsets
- `scroll-padding` on the container and `scroll-margin` on items - essential when you have a sticky header.

### Smooth anchor scrolling
```css
html { scroll-behavior: smooth; scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
```
The final project in the course left `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` and `scroll-snap-align: center` commented in its stylesheet - it is exactly this feature applied page-wide.

### Notes
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for smooth scrolling.
- Hide scrollbars carefully (`scrollbar-width: none`) - keep navigation dots/arrows for accessibility.
- Use `overscroll-behavior` to stop scroll chaining.
- Newer: `scroll-timeline` / scroll-driven animations tie animation progress to scrolling.

topics.title: Dark Mode and prefers-color-scheme
topics.summary: Respect the OS theme with prefers-color-scheme and build a manual toggle with variables.
topics.description:
Dark mode is mostly a **color-token** problem. Define colors as custom properties and swap them.

### 1. Automatic: follow the system
```css
:root { --bg: #ffffff; --text: #0f172a; --card: #f1f5f9; color-scheme: light dark; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --bg: #0b1020; --text: #e2e8f0; --card: #1e293b; }
}
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
```

- `color-scheme: light dark;` lets the browser render built-in widgets (scrollbars, form controls) in the right theme.
- The modern `light-dark()` function: `color: light-dark(#111, #eee);`

### 2. Manual toggle (user choice)
```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0b1020; --text: #e2e8f0; }
```
Toggle `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` with JavaScript and save to `localStorage`. Read the system value first with `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`.

### 3. Design tips
- Do not use pure black (#000) on pure white - choose dark gray (#0b1020, #121212).
- Reduce saturation of accent colors in dark mode.
- Use elevation (lighter surface) instead of heavy shadows.
- Check contrast again for both themes.
- Dim images: `img { filter: brightness(.9); }`.

### Avoid flash
Set the theme attribute in an inline script **before** the stylesheet paints.

topics.title: CSS Performance: will-change, contain, Critical CSS
topics.summary: Write fast CSS: cheap animations, containment, content-visibility, critical CSS and smaller files.
topics.description:
CSS performance has two sides: **loading** (file size, render blocking) and **runtime** (layout, paint, composite).

### Loading
- CSS is **render-blocking**: the browser will not paint until it has the CSS in the head.
- **Critical CSS**: inline the small amount of CSS needed for above-the-fold content in a `<style>` and load the rest asynchronously.
- Minify, compress (gzip/brotli), remove unused CSS (PurgeCSS), avoid huge frameworks you barely use.
- Avoid `@import` chains; use `<link>` and `preload` for key fonts.

### The rendering pipeline
Style -> Layout -> Paint -> Composite.
- Changing **width, height, top, left, margin** triggers layout (expensive).
- Changing **color, background, box-shadow** triggers paint.
- Changing **transform and opacity** can skip layout and paint (composite only). Animate these.

### will-change
Hints the browser to prepare a layer: `will-change: transform;`. Use it **sparingly and temporarily** (e.g. on hover/just before animating). Too many layers consume memory.

### contain
`contain: layout paint style;` or `contain: content;` tells the browser a subtree does not affect the outside, so work can be skipped. `container-type` implies containment.

### content-visibility
`content-visibility: auto;` on offscreen sections skips their rendering until near the viewport. Pair with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 500px;` to avoid scrollbar jumps.

### Selector performance
Modern browsers match selectors right-to-left and fast; selector length is rarely a bottleneck. Focus on DOM size, layout thrashing and heavy effects (blur, large shadows, filters).

### Checklist
1. Animate transform/opacity.
2. Avoid transition: all.
3. Limit expensive filters and fixed backgrounds.
4. Use content-visibility for long pages.
5. Measure with DevTools Performance and Lighthouse.

topics.title: Debugging CSS: DevTools and Common Bugs
topics.summary: A practical routine for finding why a style is not applied or a layout breaks.
topics.description:
Most CSS bugs have a handful of causes. Use a repeatable routine.

### 1. Use DevTools (F12)
- **Elements / Inspect**: select the element, see the **Styles** pane. Crossed-out declarations are overridden; a yellow warning icon means invalid or unsupported.
- **Computed**: final values and which rule won.
- **Box model diagram**: margin/border/padding/content sizes.
- **Layout tab**: overlays for Flexbox and Grid lines and gaps.
- Toggle states: **:hov** panel to force :hover/:focus/:active.
- Edit values live; use arrow keys to nudge numbers.

### 2. The checklist
| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| Style not applied | typo, wrong selector, lower specificity, later rule overrides, wrong file path |
| Element overflows | box-sizing, fixed widths, long text, 100vw with scrollbar |
| z-index ignored | not positioned or trapped in a stacking context |
| Cannot center | parent has no height, wrong axis, margin auto without width |
| Margin "leaks" | margin collapsing |
| Flex item does not shrink | min-width: auto (add min-width: 0) |
| sticky not sticky | overflow on ancestor or missing top |
| Gap under image | inline image baseline (use display: block) |

### 3. Quick tricks
- Outline everything: `* { outline: 1px solid rgba(255,0,0,.4); }`
- Temporarily set a background color to see the real box.
- Comment out half the CSS (bisect) to find the culprit.
- Validate: invalid syntax silently drops the whole declaration - check for missing semicolons or braces.
- Check the cache: hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R).

### 4. Prevent bugs
Use a linter (stylelint), consistent naming, `box-sizing: border-box`, and avoid !important.

topics.title: Project: Shaking Button
topics.summary: A button that shakes with a keyframe animation when hovered.
topics.description:
**Goal**: a call-to-action button that wiggles on hover to attract attention.

### Concepts used
- Basic button styling (`padding`, `border`, `background: transparent`).
- A **pseudo-class** (`:hover`) to trigger the effect.
- A short **@keyframes** animation using the individual `rotate` property.
- `animation-iteration-count` - the shake runs once per hover.

### How it works
1. Style the button with a purple border and text.
2. On `:hover`, change the color and attach `animation: shaking .2s linear`.
3. The keyframes rotate the element to `20deg`, `-20deg` and back to `20deg`. Because the animation is short and plays once, it looks like a quick shake.

### Improvements you can try
- Use `animation-iteration-count: 2` for a stronger shake.
- Use `translateX` instead of `rotate` for a horizontal "no" shake.
- Wrap the hover animation in `@media (hover: hover)` and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Add `transform-origin: bottom center` to make it swing like a bell.

### Why not transition?
A transition only goes from A to B. A shake needs several back-and-forth steps, so keyframes are the right tool.
