topics.title: Project: Sun, Moon and Changing Sky
topics.summary: An eclipse-like scene: a sky that changes color and a moon sliding across the sun.
topics.description:
**Goal**: a square "universe" whose sky color cycles through day and night while a dark moon passes in front of the sun.

### Concepts used
- **aspect-ratio: 1** and viewport units for responsive squares.
- **Flexbox centering** for the sun in the middle.
- **overflow: hidden** + **border-radius** so the moon is clipped to the circular sun.
- **::after** as the moon; **translate** and **scale** animated with keyframes.
- **Two independent animations** on different elements (sky and moon) with the same duration.

### How it works
1. The sky (`.universe`) animates `background-color` between warm orange and black (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%).
2. The sun is a circle with `position: relative; overflow: hidden`.
3. `.sun::after` is a black circle the same size. It starts off to the right (`translate: 100%`), passes over the sun (`translate: 0`) and leaves to the left (`-100%`).
4. At the midpoint the moon covers the sun (total eclipse) and gets a soft white glow via `box-shadow`.

### Notes
- The source code used native CSS nesting (`&::after`) inside `.sun`.
- Because both animations share a duration (8s) and are infinite, they stay in sync.
- Use the individual `translate`/`scale` properties for clean keyframes.
keyPoints: overflow: hidden clips the moon inside the sun circle
Two animations with the same duration stay in sync
aspect-ratio keeps the elements square
translate and scale individual properties simplify keyframes
Nesting (&::after) keeps related rules together
pitfalls: Forgetting position: relative on the sun, so the moon positions against another ancestor
Using px sizes that break on small screens (use % or vw)

interview.a: The sun has overflow: hidden and border-radius: 50%, so anything that moves outside its circle is clipped.

topics.title: Project: Auto Image Slideshow
topics.summary: A pure-CSS crossfade slideshow using stacked layers and staggered keyframes.
topics.description: **Goal**: a gallery that automatically changes slides forever with no JavaScript. ### The source approach The original demo animated `background-image` inside `@keyframes` (0%, 20%, 40%...) over 20s. It works, but background images **cannot be interpolated**, so slides switch abruptly without fading, and all images are requested via CSS. ### A smoother approach: stacked layers 1. Stack N slides with `position: absolute; inset: 0;`. 2. Give every slide the **same** animation (fade in, hold, fade out) with `opacity`. 3. Offset each slide with `animation-delay` equal to `duration / N`. For 4 slides and a 12s cycle: delays of 0s, 3s, 6s, 9s. Each slide is visible for ~25% of the cycle. ### Keyframes ```css @keyframes slide { 0%, 25% { opacity: 1; } /* visible */ 33%, 92% { opacity: 0; } /* hidden */ 100% { opacity: 1; } } ``` (Adjust percentages so fades overlap slightly.) ### Notes - Use real `` elements with `object-fit: cover` for content images (alt text and lazy loading). - Pause on hover: `.carousel:hover .slide { animation-play-state: paused; }` - For user-controlled sliders use scroll-snap (see Modern CSS). - Add `prefers-reduced-motion` to stop the autoplay.

topics.title: Project: Responsive Landing Page
topics.summary: Combine variables, grid, flexbox, nesting and media queries into a complete responsive page.
topics.description:
The final project of the course is a multipage responsive website. Here is its **core architecture** reduced to one page.

### What it uses
| Feature | Where |
|---|---|
| Reset | `* { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }` |
| Theme tokens | `:root { --main-color; --heading-color; --para-color; ... }` |
| rem-based sizing | `html { font-size: 62.5% }` -> `1rem = 10px` |
| Layout helpers | `.container`, `.grid`, `.grid-two--cols`, `.grid-three--cols` |
| Reusable modules | `.btn`, `.section-common-heading` |
| Nesting | `& a::after { ... }` for animated nav underline |
| Responsive steps | `@media (width <= 998px)` switches 2 columns to 1 and reorders with `order` |
| Polished details | `:is()` to group sections, `:nth-child()` for icon colors, transitions on hover |

### Page structure
1. **Header**: logo + navigation (`flex`, `space-between`).
2. **Hero**: two-column grid (text + visual) that stacks on mobile.
3. **Features**: grid of cards `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...))`.
4. **Call-to-action** and **footer**.

### Build order (recommended)
1. HTML structure with semantic tags.
2. Tokens + reset + typography.
3. Layout helpers.
4. Components (button, card).
5. Section styles.
6. Media queries (mobile-first or adjust down).
7. Test with DevTools device toolbar.

### Skills practised
Everything from the previous sections: box model, selectors, flex, grid, transitions and responsive design.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Fundamentals
topics.summary: The most common beginner and mid-level CSS interview questions with crisp answers.
topics.description:
Quick-fire answers for the questions asked most often. Practise saying each one in 2-3 sentences.

### Box model and sizing
- **What is the box model?** Content + padding + border + margin. Width/height apply to content in the default `content-box`.
- **content-box vs border-box?** border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, which makes layout math easy.
- **margin vs padding?** Padding is inside the border and shows the background; margin is outside, transparent, and can collapse.

### Selectors and cascade
- **Specificity order?** inline > id > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element/pseudo-element; `!important` overrides.
- **What is inheritance?** Some properties (color, font) flow to children; margin/border do not.
- **Child vs descendant?** `>` is direct children only; a space is any depth.
- **Pseudo-class vs pseudo-element?** State/position (`:hover`) vs a part or generated content (`::before`).

### Display and position
- **display none vs visibility hidden vs opacity 0?** Removed, hidden but keeps space, invisible but still interactive.
- **absolute vs relative vs fixed vs sticky?** Absolute: nearest positioned ancestor; relative: offset from own place; fixed: viewport; sticky: switches at a scroll threshold.
- **How does z-index work?** Needs positioned/flex items and respects stacking contexts.

### Units and values
- **em vs rem?** Parent font-size vs root font-size.
- **What is currentColor?** The element's current text color.

### Quick wins to mention
- Use semantic class names, avoid !important, prefer rem, mobile-first, and a reset with border-box.

topics.title: Interview Questions: Layout, Modern CSS and Tricky Cases
topics.summary: Layout, responsive, animation and modern-CSS questions with practical answers.
topics.description:
Mid-to-senior interviews test your ability to **choose and explain**.

### Layout
- **Flexbox vs Grid?** 1D content-driven vs 2D layout-driven. Use both together.
- **How to make a responsive card grid without media queries?** `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr))`.
- **Why does a flex child overflow with long text?** `min-width: auto` default; set `min-width: 0`.
- **How do floats collapse the parent and how to fix it?** Use `display: flow-root` or a clearfix.

### Stacking and position
- **Why does z-index: 9999 not work?** It is inside a lower stacking context; fix the ancestor or avoid creating contexts (transform, opacity, filter).
- **Why is position: sticky not sticking?** Ancestor overflow or missing offset.

### Performance and animation
- **Which properties are cheap to animate?** transform and opacity.
- **What is will-change?** A hint to promote a layer; use sparingly.
- **Transition vs animation?** A to B on state change vs keyframed, autonomous sequences.

### Modern CSS
- **What are custom properties and how do they differ from preprocessors?** Runtime, cascading, JS-controllable.
- **What is :has()?** A relational (parent) selector.
- **What are container queries?** Styles based on container size, ideal for reusable components.
- **What are cascade layers?** Explicit priority groups that beat specificity.
- **What does clamp() do?** Fluid value bounded by min and max.

### Responsive and accessibility
- **Mobile-first?** Base styles for small screens and min-width queries upwards.
- **How do you support dark mode and reduced motion?** `prefers-color-scheme` and `prefers-reduced-motion` media queries.

### How to answer
State the concept, give the one-line syntax, and mention a trade-off or pitfall.

interview.q: Why might z-index: 9999 not put an element on top?
interview.a: The element is inside a stacking context (created by transform, opacity, filter, positioned parent with z-index) that ranks lower than another context.

interview.q: What problem does :has() solve?
interview.a: It lets you style a parent or earlier sibling based on its children or following siblings, which was impossible with pure CSS before.

interview.q: How do you make a layout respond to a component's own width?
interview.a: Use container queries: container-type: inline-size on the parent and @container rules for children.

interview.q: How would you reduce layout shift (CLS) in CSS?
interview.a: Reserve space with width/height or aspect-ratio, size-adjust fallback fonts, avoid injecting content above existing content, and avoid animating layout properties.
